claims.explanation: Zolantidine is a brain-penetrant histamine H2 receptor antagonist, and the selective killing pattern tracks with dependence on histaminergic/GPCR-cAMP signaling rather than a single lineage. Lines with PTEN loss or PI3K-pathway activation (PIK3CA mutation, PTEN mutation) are enriched among sensitive lines, consistent with H2-receptor blockade further suppressing a PI3K/AKT-cAMP survival axis already rewired in these tumors. Conversely, intact PTEN/PI3K signaling or KEAP1/STK11 co-mutation may buffer against this effect, protecting lines such as NCIH1623 and NCIH1793.

features.basis: PTEN-mutant lines (KALS1, UACC62, SF126, ESS1, 8MGBA, GP2D) are enriched among sensitive lines; PTEN loss hyperactivates PI3K/AKT survival signaling that H2R blockade may further cripple
PIK3CA-mutant lines (HGC27, JHUEM2, 253J, ESS1, GP2D, MKN1) appear among sensitive lines, consistent with PI3K-pathway dependence
KRAS-mutant lines (KPNSI9S, NCIH1792, GP2D, SNU410) are enriched in the sensitive set, suggesting MAPK/PI3K crosstalk vulnerability
BRAF-mutant melanoma/glioma lines (LOXIMVI, UACC62, NMCG1) are among the most killed
CTNNB1-mutant lines (JHUEM2, U2OS, LXF289) are enriched among sensitive lines
NF1 loss (KALS1, LOXIMVI, ESS1, GP2D, SNU410) activates RAS/MAPK and appears in sensitive lines
TP53 mutation is near-universal and does not discriminate; listed as a weak/negative feature
KEAP1-mutant NCIH1623 is among the least affected lines, suggesting NRF2-pathway activation buffers drug effect
STK11-mutant lines (KALS1 sensitive but NCIH1623, SNU840 least affected) show mixed pattern; weak evidence
SMARCA4-mutant lines (COV434 sensitive but NCIH1793, NCIH1703 least affected) show inconsistent pattern; weak evidence
CDKN2A loss appears in several least-affected lines (CAL12T, SCABER, YD10B, 8305C, NCIH1703), suggesting cell-cycle arrest capacity may matter
ARID1A-mutant lines (JHUEM2, LOXIMVI, GP2D) are enriched among sensitive lines, though also present in resistant NCIH1793/KU1919
